source_text: Right so how long is this test going to take?

fragments.text: Right so how long is this test going to take?

reply_text:
Nothing is running right now; the last sweep finished. For the 54 C-authority files, measured with 4 in parallel:

| Case | Wall time |
|---|---|
| First sweep, everything runs | about 3.5 min (196 s) |
| Nothing changed | about 2.5 min (149 s), nearly all of it the two files killed at 12 GB |
| Nothing changed, if those two were skipped | a few seconds (52 checks at about 0.2 s each) |
| One test file edited | that file only, typically 20–30 s, plus the two killed files |
| A widely loaded compiler module edited | most of a full sweep (`bindings.py` reran 37 of 54) |

The whole suite is 256 test files, and I've only baselined these 54. I haven't measured the other 202, so I can't give a real figure for them. If they cost about the same per file as the C-authority ones, a first full sweep would be around 15–20 minutes, but that's a guess: 41 of them are in `implemented_by` and I don't know how heavy those are.

So the two killed files are what's keeping an unchanged sweep from being near-instant. That's the decision I left with you: record them as "killed under these inputs" and skip them, or look at why they need more than 12 GB first.
